last_summary.worked: Implemented `src/transvection_fold_slice_obstruction.py`, a new audit for affine hyperplane folds generated by one-sided symplectic transvections. The script verifies the affine transvection and normalized slice formulas, checks the piecewise Jacobian determinants, establishes the exact slice-area claim `R >= delta^(-1/2) >= 1` for any common linear symplectic left factor, and saves a report to `results/research_loop/attempt_015_transvection_fold_slice_obstruction.json`. It then runs a 5776-case nontrivial grid search over normalized fold parameters `(s,d,lambda)` and a 16-sample random audit of symplectic left factors. The identity baseline saturates the lower bound with sampled radius `1.0`. The best nontrivial refined slice radius is `1.001083448194763` at `(s,d,lambda) = (1.0, 0.9, -0.125)`, with sampled slice area `3.141591421511218` within `1.24e-6` of `pi`. In the mixed audit, the plane coefficient `delta` ranges from `0.2120672840914635` to `0.9834665528801642`, the theoretical lower bound ranges from `1.0083706647215258` to `2.1715166455758785`, the minimum sampled radius is `1.4699275946793848`, the minimum sampled gap above the theoremic bound is `0.1847597220009214`, and the maximum symplectic error of the sampled mixers is `7.080145363731219e-16`.
last_summary.did_not_work: This more flexible transvection-fold family still does not make the proposed solution correct. The central active slice `D = B^4(1) ∩ E` survives every normalized fold and every common linear symplectic left factor `L` as a planar subset of `L(E)` with symplectic area `pi`. Therefore any containing Euclidean 4-ball must satisfy `R >= delta^(-1/2) >= 1`, where `delta = |omega(f1,f2)|` for an orthonormal basis of `L(E)`. So no member of this family can act as a genuine one-ball compressor. Common linear mixing does not evade the obstruction; unless `L(E)` remains a complex line, it strictly worsens the lower bound because `delta < 1`. A naive attempt to extend the same area-`pi` argument to arbitrary linear pre-factors failed under random pre/post audit, so pre-mixing remains unresolved rather than ruled out.
